The Meadow

Three chapters: The Thicket Breaks · First Steps · Meadow Names

The Meadow · a chapter

The Thicket Breaks

The thicket was very quiet on the morning Bambi was born. He lay in a soft hollow of grass and fern, no bigger than a loaf of warm bread, and the light came down through the leaves in green and golden pieces.

His mother stood over him and washed him with her tongue until his coat shone. “You are my little prince of the forest,” she whispered.

Bambi opened his eyes, and the whole world was new. It smelled of rain and warm leaves. A drop of dew hung on a fern above him, shining, and in it the whole thicket swam, upside down and beautiful.

He did not know his name yet. He only knew the soft sound of his mother breathing, and that he was exactly where he belonged.

The Meadow · a chapter

First Steps

“Come,” said his mother, when the sun stood higher. “Try your legs, little one.” Bambi pushed — and wobbled — and his legs went every way at once, like four young saplings in a wind.

Down he sat, surprised. The fern brushed his nose. Somewhere above, a thrush was watching, and the thrush said nothing at all, politely.

Then — all at once, the way spring does everything — he was standing. Four legs, one small fawn, upright in a square of sunlight. The thicket held its breath.

The thrush sang one clear note, as if to say: look, look. The little prince is up.

The Meadow · a chapter

Meadow Names

Beyond the thicket's edge, the world opened wide. The meadow rolled away in green waves, spangled with buttercups, and the air was full of wings and humming and the smell of warm grass.

“Everything here has a name,” said his mother. “You will learn them by listening. The grass first. Then the wind. Then your own heart.”

A butterfly rose from the clover, gold as a fallen sunbeam, and danced where it pleased. Bambi forgot his wobbly legs. He forgot everything but the dancing light.

And he took one brave step after it — the first step he ever chose for himself.

You found the butterfly. It dances, and Bambi dances after it — that is how the meadow says hello.

Rainwake Orchard — a listening place

Rainwake Orchard, at night. Bambi comes here to listen. Tap the water — softly, softly — and hear the ripples answer.
